title: Introduce persona-driven RAG playbook + isolated tool-sandbox quickstart
author: Elena Park
commits: a1b2c3d: add initial persona playbook and quickstart scaffold
d4e5f6g: implement tool-sandbox README, sanitation checks, and telemetry hooks
h7i8j9k: update docs build config and snippet formatting
l0m1n2o: address review feedback (privacy phrasing, CI lint fixes)
description:
Summary: Adds a short, practical quickstart that demonstrates a persona-driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) workflow plus an isolated 'tool-sandbox' pattern for safe tool-calling in examples. Motivation: Customers build agents with personas (tone, role constraints) and often need safe local tooling examples that demonstrate sandboxing strategies, telemetry hooks, and policy gates. This PR provides a doc-first quickstart plus lightweight example artifacts that are easy to copy into customer projects.

What changed (single continuous string): The PR introduces two main artifacts: (1) docs/guides/persona-driven-rag.md — a conceptual guide on designing personas (constraints, prompt scaffolding, evaluation checks) and a recommended template for persona manifests and prompt templates; (2) docs/quickstarts/persona-sandbox-quickstart.md — a step-by-step quickstart that walks through: how to wire retrieval, apply a persona manifest for structured prompts, enable streaming, and configure a minimal tool-sandbox that proxies external calls through a policy layer. Examples are included under examples/rag/: persona-templates contains JSON manifests (persona name, safety constraints, system_prompt, allowed_tools), and tool-sandbox contains a tiny Node example demonstrating a local HTTP shim that validates tool inputs, logs telemetry events to the SDK, and returns deterministic responses for tests.

Checklist (author): - [x] Quickstart narrative and commands (mkdocs-staging build tested) - [x] Persona templates (3 variants: assistant, reviewer, domain-expert) - [x] Tool-sandbox example with input sanitizer and circuit-breaker - [x] Basic telemetry hooks (span start/end, event annotations) - [x] Security guidance section and recommended policy snippets - [x] CI docs build passes 

Testing & CI: The docs site build (mkdocs) and linkcheck passed in CI. The examples include a tiny smoke test in examples/rag/tool-sandbox/README.md describing how to run the shim and simulate tool calls; this was executed locally during review. The CI job .github/workflows/docs-deploy.yaml was updated to add a docs-only smoke step.

Files changed (high level): - docs/guides/persona-driven-rag.md: new guide with diagrams and persona manifest examples - docs/quickstarts/persona-sandbox-quickstart.md: new quickstart with copy-paste snippets - examples/rag/persona-templates/*.json: three persona manifests (assistant.json, reviewer.json, expert.json) - examples/rag/tool-sandbox/README.md & sandbox code snippets: simple Node/TS shim demonstrating input validation and a stubbed outbound call - static/snippets/sandbox-instrumentation.ts: telemetry helper used in docs snippets - mkdocs.yml & docs CI workflow: include new pages in nav and ensure formatting rules

Security & privacy notes: The tool-sandbox pattern is intentionally local and non-production: examples use deterministic, sanitized outputs and explicit disclaimers. The guide includes a "Policy gates" subsection recommending server-side validation, rate limiting, and credential isolation when moving to Dedicated or Private deployments. We added a short checklist for customers to audit tool connectors before production.

Usage example (from quickstart): 1) cp examples/rag/persona-templates/assistant.json my-project/persona.json 2) start the sandbox: node examples/rag/tool-sandbox/server.js --port 4001 3) run the quickstart script: ./scripts/run-persona-quickstart.sh --persona ./my-project/persona.json 4) observe telemetry events in the Redwood Console (quickstart points to a demo telemetry dataset)

Backward compatibility: Docs-only change; no breaking API changes. When customers copy the sandbox shim into production they must upgrade to the platform's recommended secure connectors.

Related work & references: ENG-3121 (persona evaluation scaffolding), PM-487 (developer experience content for quickstarts), SUP-908 (support ticket requesting safer examples for tool-calling).

Merge notes: Squash merge to keep history tidy. The PR includes extensive inline examples; we intentionally keep code snippets short and link to full examples in the repo to avoid bloating the docs site.

Author contact: Elena Park (docs, eng-evangelism) for follow-ups.
